items.title: The Iran War Is Creating Winners and Losers: Lockheed Martin (LMT) vs. American Airlines (AAL)
items.summary: American Airlines Group Inc. (NASDAQ:AAL) and Lockheed Martin Corporation (NYSE:LMT) Corporation (NYSE:LMT) both reported earnings the same day this week. Both companies are being shaped by the same event, the ongoing war involving Iran. Nonetheless, one firm is getting hurt by it, and the other is getting a big boost, and their stock moves on […]

items.title: US and Japan join Philippines for South China Sea military drills
items.summary: Investing.com -- The United States and Japan joined the Philippines for five days of maritime exercises in the South China Sea as Manila and Beijing traded accusations over several confrontations in the disputed waters, Reuters reported.

items.title: Russian attack on Kyiv triggers fires across Ukrainian capital
items.summary: Investing.com -- Falling debris from an overnight Russian attack triggered fires in at least three districts of Kyiv early Sunday, Reuters reported, citing Mayor Vitali Klitschko.

items.title: The 3.4% Income Play That Beats the Dogs of the Dow Strategy
items.summary: Applying the Dogs of the Dow logic across the entire S&P 500 sounds like a recipe for chasing troubled dividends, but a holding-by-holding look at SDOG reveals a more complicated picture, with two positions that deserve serious scrutiny before you commit capital.

items.title: Defense Earnings Show Readiness Now and Modernization Ahead
items.summary: Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, and RTX posted record backlogs and raised guidance this week, driven by both near-term missile defense demand and long-term military modernization programs.

items.title: Defense tech investors thought the war in Iran could make them millionaires. Instead, they faced a Wall Street bloodbath
items.summary: Firms like Northrop Grumman are struggling on the market despite record military spending. Investors are now watching Congress—and a new generation of startups.

items.title: Boeing Has a $695B Backlog and Analysts See 29% Upside. Should You Buy Before July 28 Earnings?
items.summary: Boeing carries a backlog that dwarfs its entire market value, and analysts see nearly 30% upside heading into a July 28 earnings report where prediction markets already favor a beat. The question is whether the turnaround has finally reached the point where the numbers do the convincing.
